messages:
erika: paging SRE, we're seeing a sudden latenc y cliff on hosted inference for a subset of model variants. dashboards show continuous-batching queue depth skyrocketed and KV cache growth. 5xxs for some requests.

sam: noticed increased p50->p99 gap, p99s up to 18s for stream responses. correlation with recent change to batching defaults (max_batch_tokens bumped in canary earlier).

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-194567 (sev=high) — continuous-batching misconfig + KV cache growth. Channel: #incidents. Pager: oncall-sre.

maya: root cause hypothesis — a bad config pushed to the runtime config service in the last deploy increased max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 16384 and max_num_seqs from 8 -> 64 for the cont-batch queue. That made batching try to pull huge prefixes and triggered KV cache thrash / OOM-ish behavior on some hosts.

jordan: confirmation: logs show many batch windows waiting full timeouts with hundreds of pending seqs; the router started coalescing long sequences and we ended up with long KV cache retention and page churn.

erika: customer-impact: CUST-Alpha reported degraded interactive experience (token streaming stalls, re-renders). Support team triaged ticket #6571. Might be sensitivity for low-latency chat apps.

oncall-sre: I'm on it. immediate mitigation plan: 1) rollback the runtime config change (set max_batch_tokens back to 2048, max_num_seqs to 8) 2) temporarily disable continuous batching for affected model variants 3) purge KV cache on nodes that show >90% cache occupancy 4) increase request timeout guard to fail fast for pathological batches.

ops-bot: deploy requested: runtime-config-service:rollback:1945678901 by oncall-sre — status: in_progress.

sam: adding a small hotfix to the autoscaler so it won't scale down mid-purge. also will add a safety cap on TTL for KV entries during this window.

jordan: commands I'm running on the runtime fleet (snippet):
```
# set conservative batching parameters
curl -XPOST https://runtime-config.internal/api/v1/configs/cont_batch -d '{"max_batch_tokens":2048,"max_num_seqs":8,"max_wait_ms":20}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
# toggle continuous batching off for model foo-*
curl -XPOST https://runtime-config.internal/api/v1/flags -d '{"model:foo": {"continuous_batching": false}}'
```

maya: performing KV cache purge on nodes with >85% occupancy. running sequentially to avoid a stampeding purge.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigation in progress. Explainer: misconfigured cont-batch defaults introduced during canary that increased batch sizes by 8x and caused cache/paging regressions.

erika: ops note: please watch request timeout and error budgets for next 30m. open a status page incident if customer impact persists >20m.

oncall-sre: purge done on 12/20 nodes, dropped cache occupancy from ~94% -> 34% on those hosts. rolling restart of runtime workers on hot hosts started.

customer-success: notified CUST-Alpha and posted preliminary update: "we're aware of streaming degradations, mitigation in progress; minimal data exposure risk, no data loss." They want ETA for full recovery.

sam: quick followups: 1) add config validation to runtime-config-service to block max_batch_tokens > 8192 for prod 2) add alert if average payload size * max_num_seqs > X for queueing policy 3) add a canary gate that simulates KV pressure post-config-change.

jordan: rolled a targeted config rollback to prod at +9m. ops-bot shows runtime-config-service:rollback:done.

ops-bot: job runtime-worker-restart triggered by oncall-sre — 12 workers restarted sequentially.

maya: disabling continuous batching for affected variants completed. initial latency numbers improving: p99 down from 18s -> 1.8s on rollouts where config rollback happened. still monitoring tail latencies.

erika: good. let's record this in postmortem: root cause = misapplied conservative-avoidance change in canary that was supposed to reduce batching latency but had inverted parameter math (units bug). Contributing factors: no config upper-bound validation, missing KV pressure canary, autoscaler scaling during purge.

oncall-sre: handoff to night oncall in ~30m. I'll write runbook steps and current state. Current severity: reduced to medium, customer-impact partial but improving.

jordan: runbook excerpt (to paste in the ticket):
- If p99 > 5s and batch queue depth > 1000: immediately rollback cont-batch params to safe defaults.
- If KV cache occupancy > 85%: perform staggered purge node-by-node.
- If purge time > 15m: pause continuous batching and escalate.

erika: +1 on runbook. Also please add a monitoring dashboard tile: "cont-batch effective batch size" and alert when it changes by >2x within 5m.

incident-bot: Incident INC-194567 update: mitigations applied, partial customer impact, ongoing monitoring. Next update in 15m or on significant change.

customer-success: CUST-Alpha acknowledges update, will monitor. They asked about a postmortem and ETA; told them we will follow up with timeline after full verification.

oncall-sre: handing off to night-oncall: @maya will take over. state: rollback completed, continuous batching disabled for affected variants, KV cache purges done on hot nodes, p99 trending ~1.2s cluster-wide. keep an eye on error budget and support tickets.

maya: taking handoff. leaving checklist in the ticket and will coordinate final verification and postmortem writeup tomorrow.

erika: thanks team. please file the incident doc and include code diff that introduced the bad defaults. we'll schedule a retro with runtime + config-service owners. :ear-of-rice::coffee:
